title: Can I arrive Thursday morning instead?

boundaries.note: Natural-language traveller request through the deterministic NL intake interpreter
Planning evidence from a REPLAY flight.search recording for the home/event corridor

steps.description: Traveller asks in natural language for a Thursday-morning arrival; the deterministic interpreter extracts the arrive-by window

body.text: Hi! I have things to wrap up in Chiang Mai on Wednesday. Can I arrive by 2026-10-01T09:00:00+08:00 instead? My first session is the search chat on Thursday afternoon.

assert.description: the NL request is accepted
the request came from interpretation, not a pre-structured target
arrive-by text maps to a trip-window adjustment
no binding language: the request stays a preference, not an instruction
a recovery case opens for the request
the resolver records an honest implication instead of fabricating one
the governing funding rule speaks before any window comparison: the payer decision is derived from policy evidence
the missing arrival evidence is recorded as uncertainty
the trip has no transport leg yet; the window shift is not derivable at intake

assert.expected: no derivable implications for the supplied target shape
assert.description: with no existing legs there is no arrival delta to compare; absence is recorded, never invented

steps.description: Planning loop searches the home/event corridor (REPLAY evidence) and judges every candidate against the programme arrival constraints

assert.description: the planner requests corridor evidence first, then proposes from it
a read-only tool round actually ran
the evidence request is a flight search
the REPLAY recording supplied corridor offers
every normalized corridor offer becomes a candidate strategy

assert.expected: Book a flight to arrive by the requested time
assert.description: the candidate books a new arrival on the home/event corridor, not a rebook of an existing leg
a Thursday-morning arrival deterministically violates the programme arrival constraints
the rejection carries deterministic constraint evidence
the verdict comes from a HARD constraint evaluation
the arrival-before-commitment gap is negative: FAIL, not UNKNOWN
the later Thursday offer fails the same programme constraints
hard-infeasible candidates can never win: no best strategy is ranked
the case advanced through the planning stage

steps.description: Observe the recovery case after planning

assert.description: the case belongs to the requesting traveller's trip
